business_scope.primary_industry_name: Online Merchandising of Fashion Jewelry and Fine Timepieces

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (federal codified system with a Germanic doctrinal foundation, complemented by federal commercial and financial market statutes)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Agreement between the Swiss Confederation and the People's Republic of China on the Promotion and Reciprocal Protection of Investments (signed 16 November 1986, in force 13 March 1987)
Agreement between the Swiss Confederation and the People's Republic of China for the Avoidance of Double Taxation with respect to Taxes on Income (signed 25 September 2013, in force 19 December 2014)
Free Trade Agreement between the EFTA States and China (signed 21 June 2013, in force 1 July 2014)
Convention establishing the European Free Trade Association (EFTA, Vaduz Convention of 21 June 2001)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Federal Act on Combating Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing (Anti-Money Laundering Act, AMLA; SR 955.0) as revised with effect from 1 July 2023 and 1 January 2024; Ordinance on the Anti-Money Laundering Act (AMLO; SR 955.01); Beneficial Owners Ordinance (BOV-UST; SR 221.524.1) establishing the federal Transparency Register of Beneficial Owners; Swiss Code of Obligations (CO; SR 220), Arts. 626, 626a, 627, 837 and 950; Federal Act on the Commercial Register (HRegG; SR 221.411) and Commercial Register Ordinance (HRegV; SR 221.411.1); FINMA Circular 2011/01 on Auditing; Federal Act on International Sanctions (Embargo Act; SR 946.231) and associated SECO sanctions ordinances.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Full-color certified copy of passport of each ultimate beneficial owner and each statutory director
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National passport authority of the country of origin (copy certified by a sworn notary if original is not available)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille Convention (Hague Convention of 5 October 1961)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Police clearance certificate / certificate of good conduct for each ultimate beneficial owner and each statutory director
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent judicial or criminal records authority in the country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille, followed by certified translation into German, French, or Italian

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter confirming banking history and reputation of each UBO and of any corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Existing regulated banking institution of the UBO / shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille where the issuing bank is located in a contracting state; otherwise consular legalization by the Swiss embassy or consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of certificate of incorporation and official registry extract of each corporate shareholder (if any)
Proof of residential address (utility bill, lease, or municipal attestation) of each UBO and each statutory director
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Municipal authority or public utility provider

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory enhanced due diligence for politically exposed persons under AMLA Art. 4(3) and FINMA Circular 2011/01. Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, and authorized signatories against the UN Security Council consolidated sanctions lists, the OFAC SDN and non-SDN lists, the EU consolidated financial sanctions list, and the Swiss SECO state-of-origin and embargo lists under the Embargo Act (SR 946.231). Screening must be performed before incorporation approval and continuously thereafter using automated watchlist tools, with results documented and retained for ten years under AMLA Art. 10. The target business, being online merchandising of fashion jewelry and fine timepieces (ISIC 4791; NAICS 458310), is classified as Medium_Risk_Enhanced, requiring an AMLA-compliant KYC/IDD dossier for the Stripe and PayPal payment-rail onboarding and periodic re-screening of counterparties.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Zefix - Central Business Names Index (www.zefix.ch), operated by the Federal Commercial Register Office (FEDRO) in coordination with the cantonal commercial register offices
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name must be in Latin script and may use one or more official Swiss languages (German, French, Italian, Romansh) or a Latin-script transliteration of a foreign-language name. Under Art. 950 CO, the name must be distinctive, not misleading, and must include the legal-form designation 'Aktiengesellschaft' or the abbreviation 'AG' (alternatively 'Société Anonyme' or 'SA'). A foreign-script trademark may be included only as an auxiliary name element in addition to the primary Latin-script name.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: fintech, financial intermediary, broker, exchange, fund, asset manager (FINMA license-gated)
Swiss, Schweiz, Suisse (where misused under the Swiss Trade Names Protection Act)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The reservation may be extended once for an additional 90 calendar days (maximum total 180 days) by written request to the cantonal commercial register office that issued the reservation. If the requested name is rejected on grounds of non-distinctiveness or misleading character (Art. 950-951 CO), the applicant may (i) submit a revised name application without prejudice; (ii) file a written administrative objection with the cantonal commercial register office within 10 days of the rejection; (iii) where the objection is dismissed, appeal to the cantonal administrative court within 30 days of the dismissal; and (iv) appeal to the Federal Supreme Court (Bundesgericht) under Arts. 82-86 BGG as a final remedy. Parallel submission of up to three alternative names in one clearance batch is recommended to avoid delay.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permissible as the sole registered seat. A Swiss AG must maintain a genuine registered office (Sitz) at a physical address in the canton of registration, capable of receiving service of process and identified as such in Zefix. Pure virtual mailbox or forwarding addresses are rejected by the commercial register and by regulated banks and payment processors. Serviced-office arrangements where a fiduciary leases a dedicated physical office in the company's name are accepted, provided the company holds its board meetings and administrative substance in Switzerland.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Medium-to-high. For an e-commerce company in the luxury jewelry and fine timepieces segment (ISIC 4791, AML risk tier Medium_Risk_Enhanced), unannounced physical inspections by the cantonal commercial register authority, tax administration, or Money Laundering Reporting Office (MROS)-mandated visits are estimated to occur in 10-15% of newly registered AGs within the first 18 months of operation, particularly where average transaction values and payment-rail volumes are elevated.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff per Zefix fee schedule, approximately CHF 50-100

Statutory tariff per Ordinance on Commercial Register Fees (GebV-HReg); CHF 800-1,500 for share capital up to CHF 250,000

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Reserved capital deposit confirmation (blocked account) for the CHF 100,000 minimum capital
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Bank tariff for blocked-capital confirmation, approximately CHF 100-180

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO transparency register report preparation and filing (BOV-UST)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Federal Commercial Register Office (Transparency Register) via licensed fiduciary submission
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Flat filing fee of approximately CHF 200-250 per initial beneficial-owner filing

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed fiduciary / AML compliance service provider
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for an AMLA Art. 5-6 due diligence bundle, CHF 350-600

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified translation of apostilled source documents into German, French, or Italian
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark CHF 0.30-0.50 per word plus certification fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Hague Apostille issuance for five foreign-origin UBO documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Cantonal apostille authority / Federal Department of Foreign Affairs (FDFA)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory fee CHF 50-100 per apostille; approximately USD 250 for five documents

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark CHF 3,000-5,000 for a standard AG incorporation with medium-risk e-commerce scope in Zug, Zurich, or Geneva

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office provision and commercial substance services (first 12 months)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark CHF 200-350 per month for a physical registered office in Zug, Zurich, or Geneva

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Swiss Code of Obligations (Obligationenrecht / Code des obligations, SR 220), Articles 620-763 (Stock Corporation, Aktiengesellschaft); in particular Articles 626-627 (mandatory content of articles of association), 626-629 (adoption of articles), 630 (declaration of incorporation), 632 (registration application), 640 (registration and legal personality) and 718 (Swiss-domiciled authorised signatory); Swiss Civil Code (ZGB/CC) Articles 52-59.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt / Office du registre du commerce) of the canton of the registered seat; federal electronic filing via the eGRIS portal with mandatory publication in the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SOGC / SHAB).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of the Incorporation of a Stock Corporation (Anmeldung zur Eintragung der Aktiengesellschaft / requete d'inscription de la societe anonyme), accompanied by the notarially certified Articles of Association and the banker's certificate of blocked share capital (Sperrbestatigung).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Statutory minimum share capital of CHF 100,000 represented by 100,000 registered shares with CHF 1.00 par value each; at least CHF 50,000 of the nominal capital must be fully paid in prior to registration. The paid-in amount must be deposited in a blocked escrow account (Sperrkonto) held in the name of the company in formation ('... AG in Grundung') with a FINMA-licensed Swiss bank or PostFinance; funds are irrevocably released to the company only after the Commercial Register entry is effected.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED at the constitutive session of the Board of Directors: Share subscription: the issue of 100,000 registered shares of CHF 1.00 nominal value each, aggregating CHF 100,000, is approved and ratified; the escrowed paid-in deposit of CHF 50,000 is acknowledged as sufficient. Registered office: the registered seat is fixed in Zurich, Canton of Zurich, Switzerland; corporate purpose is online merchandising of fashion jewelry and fine timepieces. Appointments: [—] is elected Chairperson, [—] Vice-Chairperson and Secretary, [—] Corporate Officer; signatory authority is collective-by-two with residency compliance per Article 718, Code of Obligations. The Board is authorized to execute all Commercial Register filings, appoint the auditor, and open operational bank accounts.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-filing corporate name clearance and preparation of constitutional documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt) via the federal Zefix business index and the eGRIS portal; informal pre-assessment by the registry clerk of the seat canton.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Run a name-availability search on Zefix verifying that the proposed corporate name is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing entry; confirm the presence of the legal-form suffix 'AG' or 'SA' and the absence of misleading elements; obtain informal pre-clearance from the registry clerk; amend the draft articles of association to match the cleared name and statutory content requirements.
required_dossiers: Draft Articles of Association satisfying Code of Obligations Articles 626-627
Zefix name search extracts for the proposed and any alternative names
Founders' identity documents (passport or national ID) and, for corporate founders, certificate of incorporation and power of attorney
Statement confirming no conflicting trademark or registered company name
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If pre-clearance rejects the name, propose a new distinctive name or add a distinguishing suffix element and resubmit within 5 working days; name objections are resolved in the registration procedure and negative registry decisions may be appealed to the cantonal administrative court within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarisation of the articles of association and execution of the incorporation declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss civil-law notary public (Notar / Notaire) active in the canton of the registered seat.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene all incorporators before the notary; adopt the articles of association by public deed; make the declaration of incorporation; elect the first Board of Directors; acknowledge the banker's certificate of blocked capital; obtain board members' written acceptances; the notary thereafter transmits the deed and supporting documents to the Commercial Register via eGRIS.
required_dossiers: Notarially drafted Articles of Association in the official language of the seat canton (German, French or Italian)
Founders' identity documents and powers of attorney with apostille where executed abroad
Banker's confirmation of blocked share capital (Sperrbestatigung)
Board members' declaration of acceptance and evidence of Swiss domicile for at least one authorised signatory
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies defects such as incomplete capital documentation or missing mandatory articles, execute a rectification addendum to the same notarial deed; the corrected deed is re-submitted without a new filing number.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Blocked escrow deposit of the CHF 50,000 minimum paid-in capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: FINMA-licensed Swiss bank (e.g. UBS, ZKB, PostFinance) operating the formation escrow account.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a blocked formation account in the name of the company in formation ('... AG in Grundung'); wire at least CHF 50,000 from the founders' accounts; obtain the banker's blocking certificate naming the company as beneficial owner; instruct the bank that withdrawals are prohibited until the Commercial Register certificate of registration is presented; the bank performs statutory AML/KYC identification of all beneficial owners.
required_dossiers: Formation account opening application
Notarised Articles of Association (working copy)
AML/KYC identification of beneficial owners and source-of-funds documentation
Board mandate and list of authorised signatories
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank imposes enhanced due diligence owing to the medium-risk jewellery/watch e-commerce profile and online payment rails, provide detailed source-of-wealth records; if the account is declined, engage an alternative FINMA-licensed bank; the capital must remain blocked until registration and no early withdrawal is permitted.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial Register filing and publication in the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt) with electronic submission through eGRIS; publication by the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SOGC/SHAB).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Sign the electronic registration application with a qualified electronic signature; attach the notarial deed, banker's blocking certificate, board appointments and signatory specimen; confirm that at least one authorised signatory is domiciled in Switzerland; pay the cantonal registration fee and federal publication fee; upon entry, the company acquires legal personality and the SOGC announcement is issued.
required_dossiers: Signed electronic registration form (eGRIS)
Notarial public deed with Articles of Association appended
Banker's certificate of blocked capital
Proof of Swiss residence for at least one authorised signatory
Payment confirmation of registration and publication fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a completion order (Vervollstandigungsverfugung), supply the missing annexes within 7 working days; if registration is refused, lodge an appeal with the cantonal administrative court within 30 days of the refusal decision or reopen the same file after full rectification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: UID, employer AHV registration and VAT registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Federal Statistical Office (BFS/OFS) for the UID register; Federal Tax Administration (ESTV/FTA) for VAT; cantonal compensation office (AHV-Ausgleichskasse) for employer social insurance enrolment.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain the UID (Unternehmens-Identifikationsnummer) certificate using the data automatically relayed by the Commercial Register; complete employer enrolment with the AHV compensation office for salary withholding; register for VAT once the annual net turnover exceeds the statutory threshold under the VAT Act (currently CHF 100,000, subject to the 2025 reform raising the threshold to CHF 250,000) or voluntarily earlier for input VAT recovery; prepare the UID certificate, Commercial Register extract and website identity verification for Stripe and PayPal merchant underwriting.
required_dossiers: Commercial Register extract
UID certificate
AHV employer registration form
VAT registration application (portal form with turnover forecast)
Board members' identity documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the UID certificate is not issued automatically within 7 working days, apply directly to the UID Service of the Federal Statistical Office; VAT registration queries are cured by resubmitting corrected turnover projections and proof of business address; refusals may be appealed to the Federal Administrative Court within 30 days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Swiss Federal Office for Customs and Border Security (FOCBS/BAZG) - Precious Metals Control Division (Kontrollstelle fur Edelmetallwaren) for hallmarking and import-marking controls; no federal sectoral licensing board exists for pure online merchandising of fashion jewellery and fine timepieces.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No operating licence required for online retail of jewellery and watches under Swiss law; mandatory compliance applies under the Federal Act on the Control of Precious Metal Articles (SR 941.31) for hallmarking of gold, silver, platinum and palladium articles offered for sale, including import declaration of regulated precious-metal content.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Federal Office for the Environment (FOEN/BAFU) and the competent cantonal environment authority (Amt fur Umwelt) of the seat canton.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category: Exempt - no mandatory EIA under the Ordinance on the Environmental Impact Assessment (UVP-VV, SR 814.011) because the activity is online retail and warehousing without production facilities; a general building-permit environmental certificate may be required for warehouse premises.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No stationary industrial wastewater or VOC emissions are generated; compliance boundaries include waste separation and take-back duties under the Environmental Protection Act (USG, SR 814.01), the Waste Ordinance (VVEA, SR 814.600), packaging waste obligations, and take-back schemes for batteries and electrical/electronic equipment (ORDEE/SENS-SWICO) for returned consumer goods; if jewellery surface finishing is outsourced to a third-party contractor, the contract must mandate compliance with the Ordinance on Air Pollution Control (LRV) VOC waste-gas concentration limits of 20 mg/m3.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification by the cantonal fire insurance authority (Gebaudeversicherung) and local fire marshal for commercial offices and warehouses; occupational safety and mandatory accident insurance coverage with Suva or a licensed private insurer under the Accident Insurance Act (UVG), including employee safety instruction records; building structural clearance for heavy safes in watch storage areas; insurers require a certified security concept (intrusion alarm, certified safe, anti-robbery systems) for fine timepiece inventory.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (FTA / Eidgenössische Steuerverwaltung ESTV / Administration fédérale des contributions AFC / Amministrazione federale delle contribuzioni AFC), portal https://www.estv.admin.ch. For VAT and indirect taxes, the FTA is the sole competent federal authority; corporate income tax is administered by cantonal tax authorities, but the FTA administers federal direct tax, withholding tax, and stamp duties.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity deriving Swiss VAT-liable turnover (generally exceeding CHF 100,000 in annual worldwide gross turnover, or CHF 100,000 from Swiss customers for e-services) must register with the FTA through its e-services portal (estv.admin.ch) or by submitting the official Swiss VAT registration form. Non-resident entities must appoint a Swiss fiscal representative accepted by the FTA (Art. 68 VAT Act). A Swiss domestic stock company (AG) automatically receives a UID (Unternehmens-Identifikationsnummer) upon commercial register entry; the UID serves as the VAT identification number after VAT registration, and the corresponding VAT certificate (MWST-Nr.) is issued by the FTA.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election exists under Swiss law. Statutory elections include: (i) cantonal/communal tax group consolidation elections under certain cantonal tax acts (e.g., Art. 13 of the Tax Harmonization Act and cantonal implementation, such as in Zug or Zurich); (ii) VAT option to tax qualifying real estate lease transactions; (iii) election for capital contribution repayment treatment to avoid deemed liquidation; and (iv) application of hybrid mismatch rules (implemented effective 1 January 2020) under Swiss domestic law, including the optional disallowance deduction for hybrid financial instrument payments to the extent not subject to income tax in the recipient jurisdiction.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CHF 100,000 of annual worldwide gross turnover (Art. 10 para. 1 Swiss VAT Act); for foreign suppliers of digital services or e-commerce to Swiss consumers, the same CHF 100,000 threshold applies to turnover generated from Swiss customers. Registration is optional below threshold but required once exceeded.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Switzerland does not currently mandate real-time electronic fiscal clearance or digital stamping. Electronic invoices are legally accepted provided the authenticity, integrity, and readability of the invoice are maintained (Art. 37 VAT Act). VAT returns and relevant reporting must be filed electronically through the FTA's e-services portal. No government clearance API or stamp is required; however, the Swiss QR-bill standard facilitates electronic processing for B2C payments, but it is not a tax clearance mandate.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods (including fashion jewelry and fine timepieces) qualify for the 0% Swiss VAT rate where (i) the goods are physically transported out of Switzerland by the supplier, the purchaser, or a third party; (ii) the export is evidenced by a valid customs declaration in accordance with Art. 23 Swiss VAT Act; and (iii) the supplier retains sufficient documentary proof (export declaration, transport documents, commercial invoices) in its records for at least 10 years. Certain services directly facilitating export and certain offshore services meeting the use-and-enjoyment outside Switzerland test may also be zero-rated. The zero-rating claim is subject to substantiation at audit; incorrect or fraudulent claims trigger reassessment and penalties.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Swiss customs export declaration (electronic via EZV/NCTS or validated customs entry, e.g., AUS/ZELV record)
Bill of Lading or airway bill (or CMR for road transport) evidencing physical departure from Switzerland
Commercial invoice of the exported goods, including full description, quantity, and export value
Proof of delivery to the foreign consignee (e.g., signed delivery note, foreign customs entry record, courier confirmation)
Inward remittance certificate or bank/FX settlement record showing receipt of payment from the overseas buyer in the original currency
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Fraudulent, abusive, or insufficiently substantiated zero-rating claims are subject to retrospective VAT assessment, late payment interest (statutory rate generally 4-5% per annum), and administrative fines of up to three times the evaded tax (Art. 86 Swiss VAT Act). Willful tax evasion or organized fraudulent activity may trigger criminal prosecution with imprisonment or additional monetary penalties. Records must be retained for 10 years; the burden of proof lies on the supplier to demonstrate entitlement to the export exemption.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Swiss National Bank (SNB) – Schweizerische Nationalbank / Banque nationale suisse / Banca nazionale svizzera; foreign exchange and cross-border payment statistics are collected under the National Bank Act, the Foreign Exchange Ordinance, and the Swiss Code of Obligations. Ancillary regulatory authorities include the Swiss Financial Market Supervisory Authority (FINMA) for banking/AML conduct, the State Secretariat for International Finance (SIF) for international financial-market policy, and SECO for export controls and sanctions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Switzerland maintains unrestricted current-account and capital-account convertibility under the Swiss Constitution and Art. 3 of the Federal Act on Currency and Payment Means. There are no exchange controls, no mandatory prior licensing for cross-border payments, and no restrictions on invoicing in foreign currency, holding foreign-currency accounts, or repatriating profits. Dividends, interest, royalties, management fees, and loan repayments may be freely remitted internationally, subject only to the 35% Swiss anticipatory withholding tax on dividends/distributions (reduction or refund available under double-taxation treaties or for Swiss-resident beneficial owners) and to the Swiss bank's standard documentary due-diligence requirements. E-commerce proceeds from fashion jewelry and fine timepieces may be collected in CHF, EUR, USD, GBP, or other freely convertible currencies with no central bank conversion requirement.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Switzerland imposes no statutory surrender, repatriation, or mandatory conversion quota for export receipts. Export proceeds may be retained abroad or converted freely. However, all Swiss banks must, under the Anti-Money Laundering Act (AMLA) and the CDB 20 Due Diligence Agreement, identify the economic purpose and origin of funds for cross-border commercial transactions and report statistical payment particulars to the SNB where applicable (e.g., Swiss International Financial Reporting guidelines). No specific percentage of export proceeds must be converted to CHF.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (Blocked Account for share capital) + Operational CHF/EUR/USD current accounts with multi-currency sub-ledgers
Capital Escrow Account under notary instructions + Operational Account with e-banking API for treasury integration
Operational Account (CHF/EUR) + Capital Escrow Account via local Raiffeisen bank branch

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: PostFinance AG (regulatory-owned financial services company; systemically relevant payments infrastructure)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (CHF) with SEPA-compatible EUR collection facilities; not typically used for notarized capital escrow due to institution-specific onboarding policies

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Conditional (peripheral collection channel, not a primary treasury rail). Swiss fintech companies holding a FINMA fintech license (Art. 1b Banking Act) may accept client deposits up to CHF 100 million on a non-interest-bearing basis and provide e-wallet accounts and FX conversion, subject to a valid banking relationship with a settlement bank. Offshore digital EMIs (e.g., EEA EMI licenses) are legally usable to collect card payments and process online marketplaces, but they cannot replace a Swiss resident bank account for statutory capital and tax purposes. A Swiss AG should maintain a licensed Swiss bank account as the principal treasury anchor, use the EMI only for card acquiring / split-settlement routes, and ensure the EMI has applicable payment institution authorization plus LSW/FATF status, otherwise Swiss banks may reject downstream transfers as high-risk.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a Swiss Aktiengesellschaft in the high-value jewelry/watches e-commerce sector, Swiss banks generally require an in-person or equivalent regulated-identity interview with the legal representative and all ultimate beneficial owners regarding CDB 20 and AMLA obligations. Physical attendance at a Swiss bank branch or a recognized Swiss notary public with original documents is the standard for high-risk industries; in limited cases, a video-based onboarding is permitted where the bank performs an identity verification service approved by its compliance department, including biometric passport verification and apostilled corporate documents. For this specific scope (ISIC 4791, online fashion jewelry and fine timepieces, medium-risk-enhanced AML), the simultaneous presence of the director at a Swiss branch is strongly recommended at account opening or within an initial 30-day compliance meeting; remote onboarding will likely be declined by tier-1 institutions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: E-commerce operations concentrated in high-risk or sanctions-sensitive jurisdictions (e.g., sale of luxury watches to countries under FATF monitoring or Swiss SECO sanctions)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Commercial register extract and status certificates; valid passport / ID of all authorized officers and UBOs; beneficial owner register excerpt (register of ultimate beneficial owners); license/authorization of the e-commerce platform (Stripe/PayPal merchant agreements); proof that no transaction originates from sanctioned persons or embargoed countries via automated sanctions-screening screenshots; shipping agreements with freight forwarders including customs and export declarations for each jurisdiction; SECO export-control permit or negative statement for any restricted product; manufacturer invoices proving legal acquisition of luxury goods; insurance and transport documents; annual audited financial statements (if applicable); and AML source-of-funds declaration of initial capital.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High level of third-party payments, platform split settlements, and digital-wallet flows through Stripe/PayPal without direct customer transparency
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Up-to-date PSP merchant account terms, verification screenshots, KYC file from the EMI/payment service provider; detailed transaction reconciliation showing each incoming settlement from processors attributable to named customers and order numbers; signed e-commerce terms of use and privacy policy; order confirmation emails and invoices; evidence of payment-intent flows; proof of customer refund and dispute handling; tax filings (VAT/GST and income tax returns) demonstrating economic substance; and a sworn compliance declaration by the director that the payment structure is not being used to disguise third-party funds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital escrow request for newly formed AG with minimum share capital of CHF 100,000 where fifty percent paid-up (CHF 50,000) and the source of funds is not self-evident
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized articles of association; subscribed capital schedule; debut and final proof of funds via bank statements showing the shareholders' own financial resources; salary slips or liquidation proceeds / sale-of-asset agreements for shareholders; Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV) tax clearance or confirmation of no outstanding tax liabilities; auditor's confirmation of share capital paid-up and at the free disposal of the board if required under Art. 733 CO; power of attorney and beneficial-owner register excerpt; and additional assurance letter from the notary that the deposit is held in a blocked account in the bank's name.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Equity capital injections into the Swiss AG must be wired via SWIFT MT103 or MT202 to the bank's blocked account in the name of the company, identified with the purpose code for direct investment equity (e.g., 'Direct Investment – Equity Capital' under the Swiss balance-of-payments reporting classification). The payment reference must include the company name, commercial register number, and the notarial file reference. A bank confirmation of a blocked account in the name of the company is issued to the notary/registry before registration of the capital increase. Shareholder loans are routed similarly as 'Direct Investment – Loan Capital' with a signed subordination and interest-rate document. No SNB prior authorization is required because Switzerland has no exchange controls. For foreign-currency conversions, the bank executes the conversion to CHF at the prevailing market rate and no notification to the central bank is required unless the payment exceeds the SNB's monthly statistical reporting threshold for banks.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements with overseas suppliers (e.g., watch manufacturers, jewelry workshops, packaging vendors) use the following rails: (1) SWIFT MT103 customer credit transfer for CHF/USD/GBP and any non-SEPA currency via correspondent banking; (2) SEPA Credit Transfer (ISO 20022 pain.001) for EUR payments to beneficiaries within SEPA including EU and EEA countries; (3) CH-Interbank Clearing (SIC) and EURO SIC for same-day CHF/EUR domestic settlements; (4) Commercial Letters of Credit (documentary credits under UCP600) via SWIFT MT700/MT707 for high-value purchases from manufacturers, with confirmed/irrevocable LCs when required; and (5) mass payout files (pain.008) for recurring royalty/artist payments to designers or small workshops. For online sales, card acquiring settlements from Stripe/PayPal are swept into the operational account through the PSP's local acquiring or cross-border SWIFT transfer; FX conversion for multicurrency disbursements can be executed internally with the bank's e-trading platform.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX Forwards (vanilla, EUR/CHF, USD/CHF, GBP/CHF) used for transactional trade-flow hedging without speculative intent
FX Options (plain vanilla, calls/puts) on EUR/CHF, USD/CHF, and GBP/CHF for risk mitigation of large expected settlements
Cross-Currency Swaps (fixed or floating, principal-exchanged) for long-term financing, shareholder loans, or balance-sheet conversion

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) – permissible in Switzerland as a hedging vehicle for receivables/payables in non-deliverable or restricted-convertibility currencies (e.g., emerging-market currencies), but not necessary for CHF because CHF is fully convertible; must comply with Swiss financial sanctions and FINMA transparency rules for derivatives
FX swaps (tom-next/spot-forward) for short-term liquidity and rollover of foreign-currency receipts

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements and management report (Jahresrechnung) including auditor's report if not exempted
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders at ordinary general meeting; retained in company records (not filed publicly)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after fiscal year-end (ordinary general meeting required by Art. 699 CO)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors' personal liability for losses; risk of non-approval of financial statements and default distribution restrictions; administrative fines under cantonal law.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (Federal, Cantonal, and Communal) including capital tax (Kapitalsteuer) declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Tax Administration (Koordination with Federal Tax Administration ESTV)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally 6 months after fiscal year-end in most cantons; for a 31 December year-end, typically due by 30 June of the following year (extensions possible upon request)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment interest (4.5%-5% p.a.), procedural fines per cantonal tax act, default assessment based on prior years; tax evasion penalties up to three times the evaded tax plus criminal proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual beneficial owner (UBO) register review and confirmation (internal; no submission to commercial register unless change occurs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: None – register must be maintained at registered office and be available for inspection by authorities (FINMA, Swiss Commercial Register, tax authorities)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No fixed filing date; must be updated immediately upon any change in beneficial ownership; annual board confirmation recommended
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal penalties under Art. 152a of the Swiss Code of Obligations (fine up to CHF 100,000) and refusal of company transactions; exposure to professional interdictions for directors.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: VAT return – if the company is VAT-registered and opts for annual filing (for turnover below CHF 5 million) or mandatory quarterly filing above threshold; annual return due 60 days after year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For annual filings with fiscal year ending 31 December: due 28/29 February of the following year (end of March with extension)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late interest 5% p.a., administrative fines up to CHF 8,000, criminal penalties for fiscal negligence; potential loss of net-tax settlement (duty drawback).

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Full ordinary audit (Ordentliche Revision) required if for two consecutive fiscal years the company exceeds two of the following three thresholds: total assets CHF 20 million, turnover CHF 40 million, or 250 full-time employees. A limited audit (Eingeschränkte Revision) is required if the company exceeds two of the following three thresholds for two consecutive years: total assets CHF 10 million, turnover CHF 20 million, or 50 full-time employees. If neither threshold set is met, the company may waive any audit (opting-out) only with the unanimous approval of all shareholders.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Swiss Code of Obligations (Art. 957-963) and Swiss GAAP FER; IFRS permitted for listed companies and voluntary use

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the Swiss Beneficial Ownership Ordinance (effective 1 July 2020), an AG must maintain a register of beneficial owners identifying all natural persons who ultimately own or control at least 25% of shares or votes. The register need not be filed with any authority on an annual basis, but must be made available immediately upon request of competent authorities (commercial register office, tax authority, FINMA). The board of directors must update the register within 30 days of learning of a change. It is recommended to perform an annual internal review and record a board resolution confirming the continuing accuracy of the UBO register.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors and Executive Officers

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,100–3,300 per year (approx. CHF 1,000–3,000) depending on canton and service provider
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,300–22,000 per year (approx. CHF 3,000–20,000) for a typical e-commerce company; limited audit at lower range, ordinary audit at higher range

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 8.5% federal corporate income tax computed on post-tax net profit (equivalent to approximately 7.83% on a pre-tax basis); the combined Zug cantonal and communal statutory burden amounts to approximately 14.6% for a resident Aktiengesellschaft, yielding a jurisdictionally blended headline rate of 8.5% federal plus cantonal/communal component of about 6.1% inclusive of all surcharges.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Switzerland applies no general statutory tax holidays, but the following preferential regimes materially reduce the effective rate for a qualifying AG: (i) participation exemption granting 100% relief from cantonal tax and substantially equivalent relief at federal level for qualifying dividend and capital gain income from foreign and domestic participations of at least 10% held for 12 months; (ii) patent box regime exempting up to 90% of net profit attributable to qualifying patents and comparable IP rights under Art. 24b VStG-compatible cantonal legislation; (iii) R&D super-deduction of 150% of qualifying Swiss R&D costs in cantons that adopted the Swiss Tax Reform and OASI Financing Act measures; (iv) notional interest deduction on superseded equity positions where cantonal law so provides; (v) loss carryforward offset available for 7 years on federal and most cantonal bases.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulär 5 / Formulaire 5 (Steuererklärung für juristische Personen) – the combined federal and cantonal corporate income tax return, filed electronically through the cantonal e-tax portal (e.g., Zug eTax, ESTV-approved filing software) and transmitted to the Federal Tax Administration (ESTV/FTA) via the TAI-code procedure. The same return simultaneously satisfies the federal direct tax (DBG) and cantonal tax obligations; a separate value-added tax return (MWST) and withholding tax declaration (Verrechnungssteuer) are filed through the FTA online portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: 31 March of the calendar year following the fiscal year-end for calendar-year taxpayers; cantonal authorities routinely grant an automatic extension to 31 May upon request, and further extensions up to six months are obtainable for professionally prepared returns. Non-calendar-year fiscal periods are accepted where the commercial year coincides with a permitted accounting reference date and the return is due within six months of the fiscal year-end, subject to cantonal practice.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter all gross turnover from the online sale of fashion jewelry, fine timepieces, and related merchandise, net of returns, discounts, and credit-card chargebacks. Worldwide e-commerce revenue is fully taxable in Switzerland because the AG has its statutory seat and place of effective management in Switzerland; export sales to non-resident customers are taxable unless physically delivered through a foreign permanent establishment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Revenue from non-resident end-customers remains taxable in Switzerland in full; no foreign tax credit is granted unless a permanent establishment abroad is actually constituted. For shareholding purposes, the non-resident parent must separately declare all transactions on schedule Z (related-party reporting).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3 (Cost of Goods Sold and Inventory)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declare the acquisition cost of watches, jewelry, packaging, and spare parts, plus inventory write-downs and freight-in. Cost of goods purchased from related parties (e.g., a Hong Kong sourcing subsidiary) must be supported by contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation at arm's length.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident related-party purchases exceeding CHF 600,000 per annum trigger mandatory local-file documentation; the taxpayer must attach a transfer pricing schedule showing the comparability analysis and margin indicators.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter gross salaries of employed staff in Switzerland, including AHV/IV/EO pension contributions, accident insurance, and other statutory payroll costs. The deduction is allowed only to the extent the remuneration corresponds to services actually rendered and is economically justified.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Where all management and personnel are located abroad, the Swiss AG will lack economic substance and the deduction may be disallowed; any payments to a non-resident management company must satisfy the arm's length principle and be reported as a related-party service.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Claim straight-line depreciation on tangible assets (e.g., warehouse, IT infrastructure, display equipment) and amortization of intangible assets (e.g., acquired trademarks, software, payment-processing contracts) using the rates approved by the cantonal tax administration. Commercial depreciation in the statutory accounts is accepted up to the fiscal limits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Amortization of IP acquired from a non-resident related party must not exceed the amounts deductible under transfer pricing rules; a step-up on a CIT acquisition is only recognized if the purchase was made in a bona fide arm's length transaction and substantiated by a valuation report.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 11 (Financial Result: Interest, Royalties, and Foreign Exchange)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report interest income, interest expense, royalty income, and net foreign exchange gains or losses on PSP balances and bank accounts. Interest expense on shareholder loans is deductible in principle, subject to the hidden profit distribution doctrine (verdeckte Gewinnausschüttung) and thin-capitalization guidance in ESTV Circular No. 6.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For cross-border intra-group debt, the taxpayer must prove the debt-to-equity ratio (generally 6:1 for financial, 4:1 for non-financial companies) and arm's length interest rate; a deemed dividend adjustment attracts 35% withholding tax on the excess portion payable to non-residents.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 14 (Taxable Profit and Loss Carryforward Application)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Compute the commercial net profit, add disallowed expenses (e.g., excessive entertainment, unwarranted management fees, tax payments), deduct participation relief, and offset available loss carryforwards from the preceding 7 years. The federal and cantonal taxable bases are reconciled on the form's appendix.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Loss carryforwards of a Swiss AG are available only to the Swiss entity; a non-resident shareholder cannot cause the losses to be utilized by a foreign successor without risking a loss of the tax identity and re-qualification of the carryforward under anti-abuse rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Annex Part B (Significant Shareholders and Profit Distribution Schedule)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclose the ultimate beneficial owners, their percentage shareholding, and the amount of any dividend distribution made during the tax period. This annex drives the collection of the 35% federal withholding tax (Verrechnungssteuer) on distributed profits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For dividends remitted to a non-resident parent company, provide the full name, address, jurisdiction of residence, and tax identification number of the recipient; indicate whether the parent qualifies for DTA relief and whether Form 82 and a tax residence certificate have been submitted to the FTA.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the federal/cantonal return attracts, in the first instance, a reminder with a procedural penalty under Art. 174 DBG of up to CHF 10,000 and daily recurring surcharges determined by the cantonal authority (typically CHF 50 to CHF 500 per day of continued default). Late payment of assessed corporate tax carries statutory default interest at approximately 3.5% per annum for federal tax and between 4% and 5% for cantonal tax, charged from the maturity date. Knowingly submitting an incomplete or false return constitutes attempted tax evasion under Art. 175 DBG, exposing the entity to a fine of between one and three times the amount of evaded tax, and repeated or systematic violation may escalate to criminal tax fraud under Art. 186 DBG with imprisonment of up to three years for responsible officers.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 35% statutory Swiss federal withholding tax (Verrechnungssteuer) is levied on taxable profit distributions, including dividends, bonus shares with reserve capitalization, and deemed distributions (verdeckte Gewinnausschüttung) to shareholders, imposed at source on the gross amount paid or credited to persons resident outside the Swiss banking system under Art. 1 ff. VStG.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a Double Taxation Agreement (DTA) and obtain a reduced rate or refund, the non-resident recipient must file Form 82 (Antrag auf Rückerstattung der Verrechnungssteuer) with the Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV/FTA) within three years of the end of the calendar year in which the dividend became economically available. The application must be accompanied by: (i) a valid tax residence certificate (TRC / Ansässigkeitsbescheinigung) issued by the competent foreign tax authority for the relevant tax period; (ii) an executed statement of beneficial ownership (Form 82-D or equivalent declaration) confirming that the applicant is the ultimate entitled owner; (iii) a declaration that no abuse of the treaty exists under ESTV Circular No. 42, including evidence of economic substance. Where the foreign parent holds at least 10% of the Swiss company's share capital for an uninterrupted period of 12 months, most Swiss DTAs reduce the withholding tax on dividends to 0% (e.g., Germany, France, the Netherlands, Luxembourg) or to 5% (e.g., the United States under the modified protocol for substantial shareholding); portfolio dividends are generally reduced to 15%. The statutory 35% is withheld at source on the payment date, and the over-withheld amount is refunded by the FTA upon successful application.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory Swiss withholding tax of 35% applies to royalty income paid to non-residents for the use of patents, trademarks, designs, copyrights, know-how, and similar intangible property under Art. 1 Para. 2 VStG, as well as to interest on Swiss bonds, debentures, and money market instruments issued by the AG. Ordinary interest arising from commercial debt, supplier credit, and standard intercompany current accounts is exempt from Swiss withholding tax at the statutory level. Treaty reduction protocols typically cap royalties at 0%–10% (e.g., 0% for certain copyright royalties under the US treaty, 5% under the Germany and France treaties, 10% under the United Kingdom treaty) and interest at 0%–10% (most modern Swiss DTAs reduce interest on genuine financial debt, arm's length loans, or pay-though structures to 0% for qualified banks and lenders; others apply a maximum of 10%). Relief is realized exclusively through the same Form 82/TCR/beneficial ownership procedure described above, and the payment of any royalty to a non-resident at a reduced rate must be pre-approved by the FTA where the payor is a licensed withholding agent.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: A Swiss-resident AG is mandatorily required to prepare and maintain a Transfer Pricing Documentation File (Local File) under Art. 58 DBG and ESTV Circular No. 49 when its aggregate intercompany transactions with any related party, whether Swiss or foreign, exceed CHF 600,000 in a fiscal year, or where related-party loans exceed CHF 600,000 outstanding at any balance sheet date. A Master File (group documentation) must be furnished upon specific request of the tax authority where the multinational group has consolidated turnover above CHF 1 billion or where the Swiss entity's intragroup transactions exceed CHF 6 million; documentation must be presented within 60 days of an official request. The documentation must demonstrate the selected transfer pricing methodology, comparable analysis, contractual terms, functional profile, and arm's length margins.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Switzerland does not apply a standalone ESR filing statute comparable to the UAE ESR framework; nevertheless, economic substance is a mandatory condition for the recognition of the AG as the beneficial owner of treaty income and for the acceptance of intercompany allocations. The FTA scrutinizes e-commerce structures where the Swiss entity acts merely as an agent or title-holding conduit; in those cases the tax authority may attribute the e-commerce revenue to the entity where the actual functions, risks, and assets are located and may reassess the Swiss AG on a deemed arm's length profit. For the CH_AG active in online luxury watch and jewelry retail, substance is evidenced by: physical Swiss inventory, Swiss customer support, Swiss bank accounts used for PSP settlements, and board minutes demonstrating management of pricing, fraud prevention, and return logistics in Switzerland.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion via Suppressed E-Commerce Revenue
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate under-declaration of gross receipts from Stripe, PayPal, and other payment processing rails; depositing a portion of online jewelry and watch sales into foreign personal or offshore accounts not disclosed in the Swiss return; use of unregistered foreign subsidiaries to extract the highest-margin transactions while the Swiss AG reports near-zero taxable profit; or the manufacturing of false invoices and sales records for cross-border shipments.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Art. 175 DBG imposes a fine equal to one to three times the amount of federal tax evaded, plus default interest on the underpaid amount; inaggravated cases under Art. 176 DBG the multiplier rises to two and a half times the evaded tax or more. Where false commercial documentation is used to conceal income (tax fraud under Art. 186 DBG), the responsible officers face imprisonment of up to three years and a monetary penalty of up to CHF 30,000; any evaded VAT under the Swiss Value Added Tax Act triggers an additional fine equal to the tax evaded (min. CHF 2,000) and reversal of input tax deductions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and the authorized signatory who sign a false tax return become personally liable for the penal sanctions and are jointly and severally liable for the amount of tax unpaid, including interest and penalties, under Art. 754 and 755 CO. Cantonal tax authorities issue travel bans (Ausreisesperre) and asset attachment orders against directors concealing revenue abroad; conviction for tax fraud results in automatic loss of capacity to serve as a board member and extended reporting obligations under anti-money laundering rules.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Withholding Tax Evasion on Dividends and Royalties
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to deduct or remit the 35% Swiss withholding tax on distributions, constructive dividends, or royalty payments made to non-resident shareholders or IP owners; structuring a dividend as a repayment of capital or an intercompany loan to avoid the tax; selling or licensing trademarks to an offshore sister company and failing to disclose the royalty outflow.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Art. 77 VStG the AG is strictly liable for the withholding tax that was not deducted, together with default interest at the statutory rate; the FTA additionally levies a fine of up to the amount of the unpaid WHT for each infringement. Criminal prosecution under Art. 80 VStG applies where the concealment was intentional, carrying imprisonment of up to three years and a monetary penalty; the withholding agent's license to act in a professional capacity may be suspended.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Each director is personally, jointly, and severally liable for the WHT amount to the extent the company has not remitted it and the director caused or tolerated the omission; the unpaid WHT claim is treated as a privileged claim in insolvency. Persistent violations give rise to personal travel restrictions and asset freezes for the management, and criminal conviction triggers imprisonment of up to three years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Treaty Shopping and Absence of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining a registered 'virtual' office in Zug without employees, operational capability, or genuine decision-making functions; routing the worldwide e-commerce IP, inventory, and payment flows through Hong Kong or BVI subsidiaries while the Swiss AG serves as a letterbox conduit solely to obtain DTA reductions and cantonal tax advantages; failing to hold board meetings in Switzerland or to keep Swiss bank accounts as the primary settlement accounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The FTA denies all treaty benefits retroactively under Circular No. 42 and the domestic anti-abuse jurisprudence, so that the full 35% withholding tax becomes final on all outbound profit distributions; the cantonal and federal tax administrations reallocate the e-commerce profit to the entity with actual substance and reassess the Swiss AG on deemed distributions, including penalties and interest from the initial tax period. The commercial register may strike the company for lack of a lawful registered office under Swiss law.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who organize the sham structure are personally liable for restitution of the unpaid taxes, social security contributions, and withholding amounts; they may face criminal charges for fraudulent bankruptcy and mismanagement (Art. 165/166 CO) and for inciting tax evasion in a foreign jurisdiction. In cross-border practice, the authorities of the parent's residence state will likely assert CFC taxation, transactional penalties, and travel bans against the directors, and the Swiss directors may be disqualified from holding any directorship for a period of years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Misstatement and Hidden Profit Distribution
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Pricing related-party purchases of watches and jewelry at a non-arm's length mark-up such that the Swiss sales entity earns persistent losses while a related Hong Kong trading company accumulates nearly all profit; paying royalties or management fees to a foreign affiliate for services never rendered; ignoring the CHF 600,000 documentation threshold and failing to prepare a Local File or comparability analysis; or retaining excessive intercompany debt financing disproportionate to equity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Art. 58 DBG empowers the tax authority to make a retrospective upward adjustment of taxable income to the arm's length standard; the adjustment is re-characterized as a hidden dividend distribution and subjected to the 35% withholding tax at the corporate level. The company additionally faces a procedural penalty under Art. 174 DBG of up to CHF 10,000 for the non-production of documentation, plus statutory default interest on all corrected assessments; significant adjustments trigger criminal inquiries for attempted tax evasion.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly approve or sign non-compliant transfer pricing agreements are jointly and severally liable for the additional assessments and WHT amounts; in severe cases the directors are prosecuted for intentional evasion, exposing them to fines of up to three times the evaded tax and imprisonment of up to three years. The personal assets of directors may be reached where the company is insolvent and the prejudice arises from the directors' unlawful intercompany decisions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML and Counterfeit Luxury Goods Payment Trail
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Funneling payments from anonymous e-wallets, unverified PSP accounts, or layered bank transfers for the sale of counterfeit luxury watches and jewelry; failing to conduct customer due diligence and transaction monitoring where the scale of transactions reaches a professional commercial level; knowingly accepting proceeds derived from VAT fraud, organized retail theft, or online scams; or operating the e-commerce business without a bank-secrecy-compliant corporate account by processing settlements through personal accounts of directors.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Although the e-commerce merchant itself is not a licensed financial intermediary, the use of payment rails to launder criminal proceeds invokes the Swiss Anti-Money Laundering Act (AMLA); upon FINMA determination of systematic violation the company faces a fine of up to CHF 500,000 and confiscation of the criminal proceeds under Art. 70 of the Swiss Criminal Code. Individual directors who knowingly facilitate money laundering are liable under Art. 305bis of the Swiss Criminal Code with imprisonment of up to five years and a monetary penalty; conviction triggers a professional ban (Berufsverbot) applicable to any activity involving payments or fiduciary management.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The directors are personally subject to imprisonment, confiscation of proceeds traced into their personal assets, and travel bans imposed by investigating magistrates. Where the company has insufficient assets to satisfy imposed fines and confiscation orders, the directors are held civilly liable for the shortfall under tort law if their negligence or intent caused the loss; additionally FINMA may issue an order prohibiting the directors from managing any regulated or commercial entity in Switzerland.
